<a id="ReservationTables"></a>

### Tables of the service

`ReservationTables` · `src/infra.ts:102`

The reservations, and the refund of each cancelled one (its key is the reservation's); the column of a reservation's status, and the name a count is read under. Whatever the database: each dialect writes them in its own SQL.

| Case | Value |

| reservations | { name: reservations, key: id, columns: { id: text, charger: text, price: number, start: text, status: text } } |
| refunds | { name: refunds, key: reservation, columns: { reservation: text, amount: number, reference: text }, references: { reservation: { table: reservations, column: id } } } |
| status | status |
| count | n |

<a id="ProductionDatabase"></a>

### Postgres in production

`ProductionDatabase` · `src/infra.ts:316` · status: **unknown**

The database and its dialect, chosen together.

In [Production](#Production):

| Port | Answered by | Which is |
|---|---|---|
| [Database](architecture.md#Database), [Read-only database](architecture.md#ReadOnlyDatabase) | [Production Postgres database](#PostgresDatabase) | an implementation |
| [SQL dialect](architecture.md#Dialect) | [PostgreSQL's dialect](#PostgresDialect) | a function |

Context: Several instances of the service write at once, and the provider keeps the backups.

Consequences: Provisioned by Terraform with the graph's values; its statements come from PostgreSQL's dialect, which cannot be mixed with SQLite's. The prototype ships no Postgres driver yet.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| SQLite in production | one writer at a time, and the backups would be ours |

- Decided by: karim
- Chooses: [Production Postgres database](#PostgresDatabase), [PostgreSQL's dialect](#PostgresDialect)
- In: [Production](#Production)
- Follows: [Abstract Factory](../../../std/docs/patterns.md#AbstractFactory)

<a id="SqlRepositories"></a>

### Reservations and cancellations as repositories over SQL

`SqlRepositories` · `src/infra.ts:329` · status: **violated**

In [Local](#Local), [Production](#Production), [Test](#Test):

| Port | Answered by | Which is |
|---|---|---|
| [Cancellation records](architecture.md#Cancellations) | [Cancellations in SQL](#CancellationsSql) | a function |
| [Reservation reading](architecture.md#ReservationReading) | [Reservations in SQL](#ReservationsSql) | a function |

Context: Reading a reservation and cancelling one ask for the domain's records, never for SQL: the repositories turn them into statements over a database port, whichever database answers it.

Consequences: The repositories hold no driver and write no SQL: they ask the dialect port for their statements, and the database port runs them. Changing the database changes its choice (the driver and the dialect together), not them.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Statements in the entry points | the cancellation would know the tables and the dialect |

- Decided by: karim
- Chooses: [Reservations in SQL](#ReservationsSql), [Cancellations in SQL](#CancellationsSql)
- In: [Test](#Test), [Local](#Local), [Production](#Production)
- Follows: [Repository](../../../std/docs/patterns.md#Repository)
